📘 This book holds every kitchen secret videos never had time for. https://mabel-wartime-kitchen.com/v7?src=desc
💌 Join the Wartime Wisdom Circle membership, and the help keeps coming. https://join.mabel-wartime-kitchen.com?src...

Twenty-five forgotten meals, one fifth of your grocery bill saved, and a jar in the fridge — that's really where this whole story starts. This video walks through what I found in my grandmother's wartime notebook, and I promise you it's not a museum piece. It's a working kitchen system that costs almost nothing and wastes almost nothing.

You'll see the real story behind Woolton Pie, the vegetable pie that fed British families every Sunday during the blockade, straight from a real Ministry of Food recipe. You'll learn why my grandmother wrote "save the liquor" in the margins of her notebook, and what that simple habit did to my own food waste once I started doing it. And you'll see the substitutions that genuinely shocked me — an eggless cake made with vinegar and baking soda, mock cream, even mock banana made from parsnip — all of them things families leaned on when the shelves were empty and the ships stopped coming.

This channel exists to dig up the practical, forgotten know-how of the 1940s and put it back in your kitchen this week, no ration book required. If any of this makes you want to try it yourself, I'd love it if you subscribed — there's a lot more in that notebook I haven't shown you yet. 🥧🥣

Mabel Wartime Kitchen brings you the real, tested methods our grandparents used to eat well on nothing, so you can use them too.

items.title: Midnight Blackberry Vanilla Cream Soda 🫐🥤✨
items.text:
Hey Scrum chums! Midnight blackberry vanilla cream soda is a spooky season treat and an easy refreshing drink. Deep-purple berry syrup, sparkling bubbles and pale cream swirl through the glass for a simple Halloween sip with a soda-shop finish! 😍

Prep Time: 15 minutes
Cook Time: 8 minutes
Cooling Time: 30 minutes
Serves: 4

Ingredients:
Blackberry syrup:
2 cups blackberries, fresh or frozen
½ cup sugar
½ cup water
1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tsp vanilla extract

To serve:
3 cups chilled sparkling water
½ cup half-and-half
2 cups ice
4 fresh blackberries, for garnish

Steps:
1. Bring berries, sugar and water to a simmer. Cook 8 minutes, gently crushing the berries.
2. Strain through a fine sieve. Stir in lemon juice and vanilla. Cool completely, then chill.
3. Divide ice and syrup among four 16-oz glasses.
4. Add ¾ cup sparkling water to each.
5. Slowly add 2 tbsp half-and-half to each glass. Stir gently once for creamy purple ribbons.
6. Garnish each with one blackberry and serve immediately.

Scrumtrulescent tip: Chill the syrup completely before adding sparkling water to preserve the bubbles. 🥤

Creamy purple ribbons or a fully mixed blackberry soda? Tag your Halloween sipping crew and show me your glasses! Eat Scrum! 😉

items.title: Refreshing 🤤
items.text:
Cream soda is the soft drink equivalent of a warm vanilla hug in a cold, fizzy glass.

It’s a sweet, carbonated beverage whose signature flavor is vanilla (sometimes with a whisper of caramel or butterscotch for depth). Despite the name, modern cream soda almost never contains actual cream or dairy. The “cream” comes from the silky, rounded mouthfeel that vanilla creates—our brains are so thoroughly trained to link vanilla with richness that the flavor alone makes the soda taste smoother and more indulgent than its simple ingredients (carbonated water, sweetener, and vanilla) have any right to.

Its roots stretch back to the 1850s, when early recipes (one of the first appeared in Michigan Farmer in 1852) were invented as wholesome “temperance” alternatives to alcohol. Those versions sometimes included cream of tartar, eggs, milk, or other oddities to create fizz and body. By the late 1800s, patents and soda-fountain versions leaned into vanilla, and the drink we know today took shape—especially once synthetic vanillin made the flavor widely available and affordable.

Today it varies by region: in the U.S. it’s often clear or golden-tan and pure vanilla; in parts of Canada it can be bright pink and extra-sweet; elsewhere you might find raspberry, bubblegum, or other twists. But at its heart, cream soda remains that gently nostalgic, dessert-like soda that tastes like a float without the ice cream—sweet, smooth, and quietly comforting.

items.title: Big G's Legacy: Bold Red Velvet Cake with Jalapeño Heat & Burnt Butter Frosting
items.text:
Big G's favorite cake was red velvet. He loved playful moments and generous abundance. So this isn't just a cake — this is how we celebrate his memory.

Red velvet stays classic — tender crumb, vibrant red, cream cheese frosting. But we're elevating it with bold flavor that honors his spirit.

THE INNOVATION:
• Candied jalapeños bring playful heat — and their BRINE folds into the batter for tang that echoes the vinegar.
• Burnt butter frosting adds nutty depth while keeping cream cheese as the soul.
• Crispy honey-pepita praline topping, poured onto parchment and crumbled by hand, shows generosity and texture contrast.

Two 9-inch round layers, 350°F, 28–32 minutes. Internal 200°F at the center. Cool completely on wire racks before frosting.

Full recipe and bake specs are shown in the video — also in the recipe card. Drop a comment: what do you think of the jalapeño brine move in the batter? Subscribe if you want more original cake drops, made with the same chef discipline.

Tags
red velvet cake, jalapeño red velvet, burnt butter cream cheese frosting, honey pepita praline, big g legacy cake, cooking with ai, chef chaz, southern layer cake, candied jalapeño recipe, original cake recipe, 9 inch round cake

Recipe Rescue Screen (V7)
This is the closing rescue card designed so a viewer who skipped to the end can still make the cake.
Step What to do
Cake Two 9-inch round layers • 350°F • 28–32 min • cool completely on wire racks before frosting

Dry mix (whisk together, Clip 2) 2½ cups flour · 2 tbsp cocoa · 1 tsp baking soda · 1 tsp salt · ¼ tsp cayenne Creamed base 

(Clips 3–4) 1 cup butter (softened) + 1½ cups sugar creamed together · 2 eggs (room temp) added one at a time, scraping bowl between
Wet mix 

(Clip 5) 1 cup buttermilk · 1 tsp vinegar · 2 tsp vanilla · 1 tbsp red food coloring
Alternate 

(Clip 6) Into butter-egg bowl: dry → wet → dry → wet → dry, mixing between each. End on dry. Fold-in 

(Clip 7) Pour 2 tbsp jalapeño brine into batter · reserve 4–5 whole slices for garnish · fold in chopped pieces
Bake 

(Clip 8) Two parchment-lined, lightly greased 9-inch pans · 350°F · 28–32 min · 200°F internal at center · clean toothpick
Cool 

(Clip 9) Turn out onto wire racks · cool completely before frosting
Burnt butter (Clip 9) ¾ cup (170 g) raw butter, measured into the pan → golden-brown → pour into small bowl → cool to ½ cup (113 g)
Frosting

 (Clip 10) 8 oz cream cheese · the cooled brown butter · 3 cups powdered sugar in 3 pours · 1 tsp vanilla · pinch salt · paddle to smooth pale tan-cream
Assembly 

(Clip 11) Cooled layers · generous frosting between · stack · coat exterior smooth
Praline 

(Clip 12) ½ cup pepitas toasted · 2 tbsp honey · 1 tbsp brown sugar → off heat → pour onto parchment sheet → cool → crumble by hand
Final garnish

 (Clip 13) Scatter crumbled praline generously · arrange 4–5 reserved jalapeño slices deliberately
Serve Slice shows red crumb with jalapeño flecks · pale tan-cream frosting · golden praline · green jalapeño garnish
